cohort: 686 adolescent patients aged 12 to 19 years who delivered in a tertiary hospital in Romania
finding: A high rate of cesarean section (52.76%) was observed in adolescent pregnancies, potentially linked to the lack of specific prenatal care protocols for this population.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the most common mode of delivery among the adolescent mothers, with the most frequent indications being Cephalo-pelvic disproportion, fetal distress, and uterine scar from previous cesarean section.
birth_weight: Assessed but specific values not reported
